sources.title: Asset Protection and Optimisation
sources.verified_claim: Network Rail ASPRO supports third-party activities on or near railway infrastructure and manages railway-interface risk; applicability depends on exact proximity and works.

sources.title: Downloads for third parties
sources.verified_claim: Network Rail publishes asset-protection agreements, development-service templates and third-party work standards; these are process controls rather than candidate-specific restrictions.

sources.title: Level crossings
sources.verified_claim: Network Rail inspects and manages level crossings according to risk; a national crossing programme does not identify a crossing constraint at a sample parcel.

sources.title: HS2 safeguarding for developers and local authorities
sources.verified_claim: Developers should use safeguarding maps to determine whether a site is affected and whether HS2 consultation is required; exact mapped intersection is essential.

sources.title: Bakerloo line extension safeguarding directions
sources.verified_claim: Safeguarding directions protect defined land for the proposed Bakerloo line extension and require referral of affected planning applications to TfL; the directions do not themselves commit project funding.

sources.title: East West Rail safeguarding directions
sources.publisher: Department for Transport / East West Railway Company
sources.verified_claim: Current directions demonstrate that safeguarding is a mapped statutory mechanism protecting project land from conflicting development; this source is national process context, not London candidate evidence.

sources.title: Crossrail 2 safeguarding directions consultation
sources.published_at: historic consultation retained as status context
sources.verified_claim: Crossrail 2 safeguarding material shows referral of planning applications within safeguarded areas; historic consultation status is retained and not treated as a current delivery commitment.

sources.title: Living by the railway
sources.verified_claim: Network Rail explains operational works, noise and safety considerations for lineside neighbours; general proximity context does not establish an engineering constraint at a candidate.
